commits.headline: feat(sdk): the keyboard and mouse for mods, interface 1.2
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac_api gains input (the keys, mouse buttons, motion and wheel for the
tick about to run), take_input (the port's own keyboard table gives pad 0
up to the mod) and capture_mouse (relative mouse mode), added at the end
of the table so 1.1 mods load unchanged. openrac/keys.h names every key,
button and wheel direction as the web's KeyboardEvent.code does, for the
new keybind setting type; mod.hpp wraps it all, the Luau types and the
reference pages follow, and package_mod checks keybinds and…

commits.headline: feat(port): the keyboard and mouse for mods (interface 1.2)
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The platform input gathers the keys that went down, the mouse's motion,
buttons and wheel between frames; the frontend captures the cursor while
a mod asks and nothing else has the mouse (focus, the overlay, the debug
menu), and stops the keyboard table once a mod takes the keyboard. The
manifest takes keybind settings, and scripts get openrac.key, pressed,
mouse, window, take_input and capture_mouse.

commits.headline: feat(sdk): a mod reports the interface its manifest names
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac_add_mod passes the manifest's api minor in as
OPENRAC_MOD_TARGET_MINOR, which OPENRAC_MOD_DEFINE and OPENRAC_MOD_CPP
report: a mod for 1.1 rebuilt with SDK 1.2 still says 1.1, and loads on a
port of 1.1, instead of disagreeing with its own manifest.

commits.headline: feat(launcher): keybind settings and presets for mods of interface 1.2
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The launcher takes mods built for the mod interface 1.2. A keybind setting
holds up to its "binds" (1 or 2) names of the SDK's keys.h, normalized to
"KeyW,ArrowUp"; keybinds of one "group" that share an input are named in
each other's conflicts; a manifest's "presets" set several keybinds at
once and reach the Mods tab. A test keeps the names the same as keys.h.

commits.headline: feat(launcher): a press-a-key control for a mod's key bindings
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Each binding is a key cap: pressed, it takes the next key, mouse button
or turn of the wheel, Escape and Tab included; a cross clears it, a bind
already in its other cap swaps over, and one another binding of its group
has is said under it. A mod's presets are a row above its settings.

commits.headline: fix(sdk): package_mod.py takes hook points by id or alias, checked against the binding table
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A manifest's "hooks" may name a hook point by its stable id
(rac1.player.take_damage) as the SDK's docs say, or by an alias
(Hero_TakeDamage, a symbol). Each must be one the SDK's table of the
mod's games has; the archive now carries bindings/<game>.ids.lock for it.
A game without a table is checked for the names' form only.

commits.headline: feat(sdk): package_mod.py takes presets of any setting type
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A preset may now fill sliders, choices, switches and text as well as
keybinds; each value is checked against its setting's type and range.

commits.headline: feat(port): the manifest's presets are checked, of any setting type
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The port refuses a manifest whose preset names a setting it does not
declare or a value that setting does not take, as the launcher does.

commits.headline: feat(launcher): presets fill any setting, sliders included
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A mod's presets may set floats, ints, choices, switches and text, not
only keybinds. A preset covers the mod's keybinds and every setting one
of its presets names; the rest keep the player's values. The row reads
Presets when they set more than keys, Controls otherwise.

commits.author: Veradictus

A class scene (mobys/moby_<class>.tscn) gets a hidden Collision child of
its root, scaled by the class scale: a MeshInstance3D per primitive
(SphereMesh, CylinderMesh, CapsuleMesh, joint ones at the bind pose) and

triangle part, each with rc1_collision_kind and rc1_surface metadata (the
plugin's contract), coloured as the level collision's surfaces.

commits.headline: feat(editor): pack edited moby class collision into the level's core
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
pack_collision now gathers both the level collision and the class scenes'
collision before building the core: the class blobs go in first (in
place, or appended with the class header and core size following), then
the level collision block as before, and one set of level data patches
covers both. A level whose scenes are untouched still packs to nothing,
and the class scenes are only read when their manifest says something
changed.

commits.headline: feat(editor): put the Collision dock in every exported project
commits.author: Veradictus

write_project copies editor/addons/openrac_collision into the project
and enables it in project.godot's [editor_plugins]. extract.py's update
installs it in the projects it keeps too (beside refreshing rc1/), so
an earlier export gets the dock without being written again; a
project.godot that enables other plugins keeps them. The level scenes
do not change, so godot.SCHEMA stays 3: no level is replaced for this.

Tests: a fresh project has it enabled; an older project gets it once,
twice…

commits.headline: test(editor): count the cells a removed face sat in as rewritten
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The disc's tool puts a face in some cells the exact overlap test does
not count (level 14 of the PAL disc has one); those cells hold the
removed face, so their rewrite is the edit, not a stray change. Found
by running the dock's edit format on all 19 PAL levels (each: an
untouched scene packs nothing; three faces removed, repainted and
moved, a quad and a hero face, decoded to exactly the edit): all pass.

commits.headline: style(editor): comment the Collision dock's remaining branches
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
GDSCRIPT_CONVENTIONS.md asks for the reason of each branch; a few
guards in plugin.gd, level_faces.gd and dock.gd had none. Checked with
every default GDScript warning treated as an error: none.

commits.headline: fix(editor): mobys/collision.json lists every class scene, so an untouched project skips the disc
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Class scenes of classes with no class data in the core (29 on level 3, such
as moby_157.tscn) were left out of the manifest, so unchanged_scenes found
them as extra scenes and the packer read the disc's classes for nothing. Every
class scene is listed now. Checked on PAL level 3: the fast path holds, the
project imports in Godot 4.7.2 with no error or warning, check.gd passes,
and pack says no level differs.

commits.headline: fix(port): Start's skip and the movie player take the report the mods leave
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
With a mod on the pad's reports, the skip_cutscenes setting's Start (the
shoulders it adds for a cutscene, Cross for the ship, the flight's skip)
ran on the window's pad before the mods, and the movie player read the
window's pad without them: a key a mod binds to Start never skipped a
scene or a movie. The pad library now applies the skip to the report the
mods leave, and the movie player reads the pad through them. Without
mods nothing changes.

commits.headline: feat(sdk): the pointer over the game's picture, interface 1.3
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac_input gains pointer_x, pointer_y and pointer_inside, appended after
the 1.2 state: where the cursor is over the game's 4:3 picture (the middle
of a wider one), for a mod that lets the mouse point at the game's menus.
The frontend fills them, the C++ layer and scripts (openrac.pointer) read
them; SDK 1.3.0.

commits.headline: fix(editor): draw the Collision dock's drag box over the 3D view
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The plugin handles no object type, so Godot never called its
_forward_3d_draw_over_viewport and the box being dragged was invisible.
Forced draw-over forwarding draws it whatever is selected.

commits.headline: fix(editor): Alt-click picks the connected faces in place of the selection
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Alt-click always added to the selection, so it could not start a new one.
It now replaces it, as a plain click does; Shift-Alt-click adds, and
Connected, same surface still grows the whole selection.

commits.headline: fix(editor): import the class collision made from a model before loading it
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Make class collision from its model (mesh) waited for a file system scan,
which finds the new glTF but has not imported it yet, so every press failed
with "written but not imported yet" and left another file behind. The
file is now imported on the spot and loaded.

commits.headline: fix(editor): draw the selected object's class collision over its model
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A crate's collision sits inside its model, so selecting a moby showed
nothing but its box. The selected moby's (or class scene part's) collision
is now drawn over the model, the rest as before.

commits.headline: fix(editor): a class scene's Collision dock shows only its object tools
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
In a class scene the dock listed every level tool, disabled, above the
object collision, which sat a long scroll down. The level's tools are now
hidden there, and the edit report sits outside them, so Make class
collision from its model reports in a class scene too.

A hero wall selection read "10 faces selected: . 10 of a hero wall".
The legend's swatches also keep their height beside a wrapped line.

commits.headline: fix(launcher): mod rows and settings stay side by side in every webview
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The setting rows, the mod list's rows and the mod page's head were grids
that switched to one column below 860 and 760 px, so a narrower launcher
window (as on Linux) stacked each name above its control. They are now
plain flex rows (the words shrink, the control keeps its width) that
stack only below 600 px, under the window's floor. The setting rows no
longer use the class name row, which app.css also styles, and the
switch's focus ring no longer needs :has().

commits.headline: fix(launcher): find Discord's IPC socket in the macOS temp folder
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
Discord keeps its IPC socket in the user's temp folder on macOS ($TMPDIR,
a per-user path under /var/folders), not /tmp, so find_socket_paths never
found it and Rich Presence silently stayed off when the launcher ran from
`yarn tauri dev` or the app alone. The Unix path list now probes
std::env::temp_dir() before the /tmp fallback, deduplicated against the
XDG and /run/user candidates as before, and a test covers a socket that
only exists in the temporary folder.

Verified with cargo test -p…

commits.headline: feat(port): macOS Game Mode for the game application bundles
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
The game bundles' Info.plist had neither a game category nor the Game Mode
key, so macOS never treated them as games and Game Mode never turned on,
whether the game was started from the launcher or from Finder. The bundles
now carry LSApplicationCategoryType=public.app-category.games (macOS 14 and
15) and LSSupportsGameMode (macOS 26 and later); the viewer's bundle keeps
neither.

macOS still turns Game Mode on only in full screen: F11, or Borderless or
Fullscreen in the game's video…

commits.headline: fix(port): keep hostgen's Clang checks out of ccache
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
hostgen's plain `-fsyntax-only` check could be answered from ccache
when `clang` on PATH was ccache's wrapper. hostgen rewrites its prepared
copies between checks (and os.replace reuses inodes), so ccache's
direct/inode cache could return the verdict for the previous content. In
rac1-pal's pause.c that hid a conflicting declaration from the check,
while the AST dump that followed refused the same file, and hostgen
dropped the whole unit.

Run every hostgen Clang invocation with…

commits.headline: fix(port): keep each of a name's contradicting declarations apart
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
fix_from_diagnostics renames a declaration that contradicts an earlier
one and then every later occurrence of the name. When a name is
declared more than twice with different types (rac1/pal's pause.c
declares func_001F75D0 twice more), that renamed the next declaration
into the first one's alias, so the prepared copy still had conflicting
types and hostgen dropped the unit.

Collect the lines Clang names in a conflicting-types or redefinition
error, and leave those declarations untouched when…

recipe), what to watch when one fires, why the cheat codes are not a
test rig, and what is…
